 A substation transformer with a de-energized Deterministic Exact Transient Control (DETC) system is a specialized electrical transformer used in power substations to change the voltage of electricity. This transformer is designed to be de-energized, meaning it is not actively transmitting power, during maintenance or inspection, with the DETC system providing a precise and controlled way to de-energize the transformer, ensuring the safety of maintenance personnel. The main components of a substation transformer with de-energized DETC include the core, windings, insulation, oil, cooling system, de-energized DETC system, and the control panel.

The core is made up of thin laminations of steel, which are stacked together to form the magnetic circuit. The windings are the conductors that carry the electrical current, and are insulated from each other and the core to prevent short circuits. The insulation is typically made of paper or oil-impregnated pressboard, and is used to insulate the windings from each other and the core. The oil serves as both a coolant and insulator, and helps to prevent the transformer from overheating. The cooling system is used to remove the heat generated by the transformer during operation. The de-energized DETC system is a separate component that is used to safely de-energize the transformer, and the control panel is used to monitor and control the transformer's operation.

The asset boundary of this transformer includes all the components and structures that are necessary for its operation and maintenance. This includes the transformer tank, conservator, Buchholz relay, surge arresters, lightning arresters, and any associated wiring or control systems. Additionally, the asset boundary includes the rated power and voltage of the transformer, as well as any documentation or records related to its design, construction, testing, and maintenance. This information is important for ensuring the safe and reliable operation of the transformer, as well as for planning and executing any necessary maintenance or repairs.
